## [0.0.11] - 2026-11-24

### Fixed

- **A sign-in GitHub refuses is the source contract's sign-in failure on a source read.** `events_list` and `probe`
  answered a refused renewal with `SIGN_IN_REJECTED`, and a token GitHub rejects (HTTP 401) with `UNAVAILABLE`. The
  contract knows neither as a sign-in, so a consumer told the person the source was unavailable rather than asking
  them to sign in again. Both now answer `AUTH_REQUIRED`, which the contract reads as `NEEDS_SIGN_IN`, with the same
  next step. `github_api` keeps `SIGN_IN_REJECTED`. A 401 on `/notifications` still leaves the notifications out.
- **For jelly:** both `jelly.signIns` entries declare `needed: ["AUTH_REQUIRED", "SIGN_IN_REJECTED"]`, so a host can
  match a tool result's code to the GitHub sign-in without reading the next step's words (#37).

### Known limits

- **GitHub decides its tools.** The plugin's tool table follows GitHub's hosted server at this release. A tool GitHub adds later runs under `access`, is listed as unknown in `/github-status`, and is not a script method until the plugin classifies it. `npm run drift` compares the table with the server.
- **The token limits what is possible.** The scopes you granted decide what the account's token can do. The default `repo` scope reaches every repository the account can write.
- **Toolsets are a selection.** The default `toolsets` turn on 15 of the 24 toolsets, which show 69 tools. Nine toolsets are off by default, such as `copilot` and `gists`, and GitHub's two issue artifact tools need a feature flag the plugin does not turn on. See the [toolsets table](docs/configuration.md#toolsets).
- **An allow on `github_api` covers writes.** An allow for `github_api` authorises every `api` call, reads included, and also its writes, downloads and uploads. Grant it only to a session that may change GitHub, or set `access` to `"read-only"` for a read-only script.
- **Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2 only.** Other releases in `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0` run untested.
- **Agents without the base allow ask before reads.** Every GitHub request asserts `github_api` on its own `METHOD /path` first. An agent without the base `* * allow` rule gets no default block, so its `github_api` reads ask, and a script's reads there are refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED` until that agent's rules allow them (see [Permissions](#permissions)). `events_list` is not affected: its reads assert `github_events_list`, so an allow for that tool, which Jelly writes, is enough.
- **A GitHub App sign-in expires after six months.** Its 8-hour user token is renewed with its refresh token, which lasts six months; after that, or once GitHub refuses it, `/connect` asks for a new sign-in. The App reaches only the accounts it is installed on.
- **Jelly.** The `access` and `unknownTools` settings declare their choices, which only a Jelly that includes app#1301 reads; an older Jelly refuses the plugin's declaration.
- **GitHub's rate limits and error text are GitHub's.** Errors from OpenCode and GitHub pass through unchanged.
- **`events_list` reads GitHub's search, which has its own limits.** GitHub allows 30 search requests a minute for a
  signed-in user, and at most 1,000 results for one query ([REST API endpoints for search](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/search/search#rate-limit));
  one `events_list` call makes three searches (issues, pull requests, commits) and at most 30 search requests (6 each, for pages of 100 paged by time, and one second read whole when a page lies in it), each with 60 seconds to answer, beside GitHub's REST limit of 5,000 requests an hour for a user
  ([rate limits for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api)).
  A call over the limit fails with GitHub's answer as `UNAVAILABLE`: call again later with the same cursor.
- **`events_list` misses commits that reach the default branch late, with no gap.** GitHub's commit search covers only

  kind and refused every other event at ingest, so a first read stored nothing and moved its cursor past the events.
  The three emitters now make every event kind `event`, and keep what it was in the event's `labels`: `issue` or `pr`
  first, then the state and GitHub's labels, and `commit` for a commit. A notification's kind was already `event`.

## [0.0.9] - 2026-11-20

### Added

- `github.notifications`, a list snapshot of the latest notifications the sign-in may read, for a consumer and not an
  agent: the tools RPC method `events_list` with `list` `notifications` answers the contract's `list` output, the latest
  50 GitHub's inbox holds, newest first, read or unread, once each, with the subject's title as the text and the
  repository and reason as the note. It is one `GET /notifications` through the same client as `github.activity`, not a
  second one, read whole up to 32 MB as the activity feed's notifications are. A title that holds a secret is screened
  whole and left out before anything is cut. The answer stays inside the source's 64 KB by dropping whole items, marked
  `shortened: true`. The tools RPC method declares both answers, the events page and the list, so the host accepts the
  list; `github_events_list`, the model's tool, keeps its events-only input and output, so a model sees no change.
- **For jelly:** `sources` gains `github.notifications`, so Jelly asks for consent again; `github.activity` is unchanged.

### Changed

- The source contract is `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` v0.3.0, pinned as
  `github:we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract#v0.3.0` (commit `2fd55cd`) and bundled into `dist/index.js`, still with
  no runtime dependency. `github.activity` and `github.notifications` declare and send none of v0.3.0's new keys
  (`facts`, `hints`, `routines`, actor `kind`, `sections`/`parts`), which a consumer still on v0.2.0 refuses; their
  declarations and pages are unchanged, and a pin alone sends nothing. The conformance report's new checks are not

## [0.0.8] - 2026-11-18

### Changed

- Tested on OpenCode 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, so `TESTED_HOSTS` now holds 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and
  2.3.2. The supported range is unchanged (`>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`). The host and pack stages, CI and the release's install
  check run on every one; the plugin is tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2. They need
  nothing else from this plugin: between 2.3.0 and 2.3.2 the only API changes are that `experimental.generate`
  excludes video jobs and a new `codemode` session event kind.

### Fixed

- **`events_list`'s searches page by time, so a result that changes while a search pages loses nothing.** A search
  paged by page number over results sorted by time: a result already read that changed between two requests moved to
  the end, every later result moved up a place, and the first result of the next page was never listed, with no gap.
  Each page now asks again from the last second the page before it read, up to the read's cut, and a result read twice
  is listed once; a second read whole by itself is read again from its first result when one leaves it meanwhile.
- **A search answer over 32 MB no longer stops every stream.** It answered `TOO_LARGE` on every call, notifications
  included. Its range is now read again in pages of 10, and within a second read whole, as ten pages of 10 at the same
  offsets, then pages of one. Only a result alone over 32 MB is left out, with one `gap` (`window-truncated`), and the
  search goes on after it. `TOO_LARGE` remains for a notifications answer over 32 MB.
- **A second one call cannot read whole no longer stalls every stream.** A result over 32 MB in a crowded second, with
  other searches paging in full, left too few requests to read it: it held, started again every call, and nothing past
  it was listed, with `more: true` and no gap. The next call now reads such a second first, before the other searches;
  if even that is not enough, the second is walked in GitHub's order across calls, listing what each call reads, with
  the walk carried in the cursor. At most one call in a row lists nothing because of a second, and a second of n
  results takes at most 1 + n/20 calls.
- **A cursor is at most 960 characters, under the source contract's 1,024.** A search position spelled out its item's
  id, so three positions in repositories with the longest names, with a cut, a gap and a loss, made a cursor of 1,038
  characters, which the contract refuses. A position now holds an 11-character hash of the id (a second's results are
  ordered by it), times are seconds in base 36, and positions are a list: the longest cursor is 799 characters, a walk
  in each search included. **Every cursor a release issued is still read and continued**, with nothing lost or listed
  twice: 0.0.0's to 0.0.2's (refused since 0.0.3), 0.0.3's to 0.0.5's, and 0.0.6's and 0.0.7's. Only a cursor no release could have written is `CURSOR_INVALID`.
- **A known limit, now stated:** a commit that reaches a default branch after the commits stream has passed its
  committer date (typically from a pull request merged later, or a cherry-pick) is never listed, with no gap, as in
  every earlier release. The merge of a pull request the person is involved in is still listed. See the `events_list`
  docs and the README's Known limits.
- **Each of `events_list`'s and `probe`'s requests has 60 seconds**, its answer read whole included: past that it stops
  and the call answers `UNAVAILABLE`, with the cursor unchanged. The caller's own abort still stops it at once.
- **`events_list`'s reads (its searches and its notifications) take GitHub's answers whole, up to 32 MB a page, instead
  of the 100 KB cap meant for answers shown to an agent; an answer over 32 MB answers `TOO_LARGE`.** A page used to be
  cut to the 100,000 bytes `github_api` shows an agent, and a cut page failed the read with `UNAVAILABLE`, whose next
  step asked for a smaller `limit`: that asked
